## Details

### elekloader

Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Also covers Octatrack and (proof of concept) Analog Four MKII, which are out of scope for now. Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson - the last one adds Digitakt II / Digitone II / Analog Rytm MKII support, see elekloader-simonjohansson). Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument.org and the repo (read 2026-10-31): canonical repo is github.com/elekloader/elekloader (183 commits, 103 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later); web app moved to elekloader.github.io/elekloader; the Mac app was absent from v0.9.0 because signing secrets need renewing. v0.9.0 cores: core-4.1 and core-4.1-os1.54 (Digitakt mk1), core-dn1-4.1.1 and -os1.44 (Digitone mk1), core-ar2-0.8 (Analog Rytm MKII 1.74), core-ot-0.8 (Octatrack 1.40C), core-mc-0.3 (Model:Cycles), core-ms-0.1 (Model:Samples), core-a4 0.1-0.4 (Analog Four MKII 1.56). Kit 0.7.0 catalog: 19 cores, 88 mods. machine-pages 1.2/1.3/1.5 need core 3.0+ on Digitakt mk1 and refuse NEIGHBOR 0.6, SOPHIE 1.1.13 and digichain-based machine mods beside them; fxkit 0.1 gives Digitone effect mods a shared mixer, two LFOs, pattern p-locks and a CPU guard; core-dn1 4.1 adds ev_note_queue; kit 0.6.0 gives 4.0 cores larger RAM areas (256 KB Digitakt, 1.25 MB Digitone). docs/ includes AGENTS.md, DEVICES.md, MACHINES-DN2, SHARC-DN2, CORES, FORMAT, BUILDING, ADAPTING (not all read yet - see hardware/MINING.md). The earlier irpina/elekloader repo is where the author's older releases lived._

_Sources: forum thread 30, GitHub release v0.4.0, gearnews, dubspot_

### Modwerk (formerly Octamod)

Browser-based hub, builds locally from the user's own stock OS. Browse mods by device, forum with a section per device, shared SDK. Dubspot (13 Oct): several modules are still early prototypes. last_activity = date of the Dubspot article, not a forum post. 2026-11-02: three Analog Rytm MKII modules by npp1993 moved into the library (Pipo Loop 0.1.1, Sample RATE 0.1.0, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.6.0, all experimental, OS 1.74; linkable together with core-ar2 0.7, Filter Hz and Loop Sync; the packages themselves not yet run on a unit). `_submissions/` takes no new modules. The Octatrack USB beta also works on the MKI. 2026-11-03: the site now lets you download a built Analog Rytm MKII .syx (after confirming you know how to get back to stock); new Rytm module quick-velocity-aftertouch-assign with a verification note. Zoom pedals: an effect whose group+ID clashes with one already on the pedal is moved to a free local Delay ID 958-1023 (ID only in the ZDL header at 0x40-0x41, no checksum); two effects with the same group and ID froze an MS-70CDR at boot until its ROM was reprogrammed.

_Sources: gearnews, dubspot, forum thread 36_

### elektron-firmware-tool

C, MIT licence. Unpacks Elektron .syx firmware and repacks it as a valid file. Lists Analog Heat MKI, MKII and +FX among supported devices - currently the only Analog Heat-relevant tool we found. Forum listing: 113 stars, repo created 2026-07-22, "last commit 1 month ago" at the time of listing.

_Sources: forum mod list (mods.php?id=7), forum thread 8_

### digitakt-ii-research (Deja Vu LFOs, ONESHOT zoom)

Windows standalone builder (portable, no Python/Git/WSL needed) that takes the user's own official OS file, identifies it by SHA-256, writes the patched .syx; the user installs it with Elektron Transfer. The builder never connects to the instrument and never flashes. Adds two random-loop LFO waveforms on all three LFOs: DV-F (WAVE 7, free-running) and DV-T (WAVE 8, read position resets on track trigger); MODE = 2/4/8/16/32 steps; SPH = randomness (0 new values each step, 64 locks values and order, 127 keeps values but reorders, in between blends); stock WAVE 0-6 stay on stock paths. v0.2.0-beta adds a ONESHOT waveform zoom (encoder C cycles 1x, 2x, 3.75x, turning C pans; only in the combined 1.17 edition). Hardware: all three outputs validated on a physical unit for normal boot and operation, described by the author as beta evidence, not exhaustive. Open: broad MIDI / sequencer / transport / sync regression, save-reload-power-cycle persistence, long-duration stability. Unsigned .exe (SmartScreen warns). Repo: docs/INSTALLATION.md and docs/RECOVERY.md, windows-builder/, src/dv/ (host model), coldfire/ (DV, routing, trampoline, startup-allocation source), research/ (byte-backed findings), tools/midisniff.py (passive SysEx capture, does not transmit). Evidence ladder used by the author: SOURCE/STATIC, HOST, SYNTHETIC UNICORN, NATURAL EMULATED, HARDWARE. MIT, 7 commits, 4 stars. Credits: Marbles (concept only), Bezronczek's Syntakt Firmware Workbench (behavioural reference), ElekLabs digikit (research tooling, not bundled), elektron-firmware-tool (vendored).

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument lists it as "Digitakt II All-in-One" v0.3.0-beta (2026-10-23) for OS 1.17: patches in Plaits models, DX7 banks, the Deja Vu random-loop LFO, WAVE tables and the one-shot zoom; brick-risk flag set. LICENSE CONFLICT: the repo README/LICENSE we read says MIT, altstrument says AGPL-3.0-or-later - check the repo before reuse. Earlier releases 0.2.0-beta (2026-10-18), 0.1.1-beta (2026-10-17). LICENCE SETTLED (2026-11-02, repo read): both are right for their part. The repo root is MIT; the `all-in-one/` subtree is AGPL-3.0-or-later because it is modified firmware derived from digikit (its README and NOTICE say so). The All-in-One is built with digikit's patchkit: loader in the flash cave at `0x403117c4`, code in digikit's `cf.expansion` region `0x47e8b000-0x47fe0000` (see hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md, "Three Digitakt II mod routes")._

_Related: builds on `digikit` (all-in-one/README.md: modified firmware derived from digikit; uses its patchkit); vendors `elektron-firmware-tool` (catalogue notes: elektron-firmware-tool (vendored)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: forum threads 80 and 83, GitHub README, GitHub releases, all-in-one/README.md and NOTICE read 2026-11-02_

### DN2 DT2 firmware research

Source-only recipes for Digitone II firmware with six Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE), stereo samples, sample browsing, DT2 parameter graphics and SLICES trig mode. Recorder adds recording/resampling, source selection, normalization, trimming, audition, saving to +Drive and optional track assignment; VOICE cycles Voice Setup, Sample Manager and Recorder. Class-compliant USB audio provides 42 capture channels at 48 kHz/24 bit (MAIN, tracks 1-16, DELAY, REVERB, CHORUS, INPUT as stereo pairs) and a stereo return. R012 needs only the official DN2 1.11 and DT2 1.16 OS files; silent compatibility data replaces the private sample bank, and users load their own playable samples afterward. Native and browser builders verify exact inputs and the output: 2,563,872 bytes, SHA-256 4a2742a4...63a3a9a. The browser builds locally without uploading files; neither builder flashes the instrument. No firmware images or samples are distributed. Historical exact T1E2/R003/R008/R011 builds still require their original private sample bank. R011 fixed USB publication stalling after project changes by selecting its candidate destination from current DMA START while preserving ownership checks; R012 retains that fix. Owner-confirmed stock audio, samples, Recorder and USB audio on R012, including after project changes. Stable does not mean exhaustive validation: exact trimmed-file comparison, full Recorder-source coverage, endurance and end-to-end USB latency remain unverified. Builds on dnfw (angellinares/dn2_firmware_explore), selache, digikit and elektron-firmware-tool. AGPL-3.0-or-later. 2026-11-03: README warns new users NOT to install R012 yet. R012 mounts an existing sample filesystem but does not create one on a DN2 that never had it; symptoms are 0% Free / 0 bytes in Transfer, stalled uploads, Connection failed. The author says stock FORMAT +DRIVE, EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET do not create it and can erase projects; an on-device formatter with erase confirmation is in development, not released. Owner testing had used storage prepared during development. A track-2 sample reload report turned out to be an unsaved project, not a bug.

_Related: builds on `dn2-firmware-explore` (catalogue notes: builds on dnfw (pinned commit)); builds on `digikit` (catalogue notes: builds on digikit (pinned commit)); builds on `elektron-firmware-tool` (catalogue notes: builds on elektron-firmware-tool (pinned commit)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub README, releases/r012.json, docs/recorder.md, docs/browser.md, docs/research/2026-11-03.md, docs/samples.md_

### Elek View (screen viewer in the browser)

Shows a device's screen in the browser over Web MIDI, using the stock RPC screen request (an HTML port of screendump). Tested on a Digitakt II and a Model:Cycles; the author reports an Analog Heat MKII working. Nothing else may hold the MIDI port. GPL-3.0. Found on elektronmods.com 2026-11-03.

_Related: port of `screendump` (README: a .html implementation of jakobbak/screendump) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: elektronmods.com thread 93, README, index.html_

### digikit

Native Rust emulator that runs the ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together, with front panel, display and audio, plus a web panel (WASM core), a Tauri desktop app, the patch toolchain "patchkit" (applies modules to the user's own .syx), a headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes, a control socket for patch injection and DSP/ColdFire analysis databases with Ghidra tooling. README caveats: the DSP "does not run in real time yet", the browser host is parked on branch wip/browser-host, "no patched firmware has been installed on a device", and recovery via the bootstrap menu is "not tested on hardware". patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8. 982 commits, AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra section-7 terms (attribution, origin, names) in NOTICE; page shows 46 open issues. GitHub marks it as not a fork. The org ElekLabs has 2 public repos: digikit and a fork of js216/selache. Original author: the GitHub profile m-dwyer is named "Em D" (Melbourne), which is exactly the credit ElekLabs' NOTICE requires ("digikit by Em D"); Overtone credits digikit to "Em D" as well. The earlier repo m-dwyer/digikit (196 commits, 4 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later, README at the time: "no audio", last visible file HANDOVER-2026-09-16) shows no move/archive notice and does not mention ElekLabs. ElekLabs has no public members, so the pages themselves do not show who runs it; the maintainer (user of this repo) states that Em D develops in ElekLabs/digikit (2026-10-31, not verifiable on the pages). The licence changed from GPL-2.0-or-later to AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra terms. Treat both repos as one project line, ElekLabs/digikit being the current one. Mod READMEs that say "digikit's emulator" mean this project.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument (2026-10-31): main @ 283bb90, untagged, described as patch toolchain AND run-time module system plus emulator; AGPL-3.0-or-later. Its device-side tools (dkupload, dklog) belong to that module system._

_Sources: GitHub README ElekLabs/digikit, GitHub README m-dwyer/digikit, lapin-list_

### Elektroid

Sample and SysEx manager. README device list includes Analog Heat MKI, MKII and +FX, Digitakt I and II, Digitone I/II/Keys, Syntakt (also Analog Four/Rytm/Keys, Model:Cycles/Samples, Monomachine MKII). GPL-3.0, 2,506 commits, 425 stars. No version/date visible.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: v3.4 (2026-08-22) adds Syntakt samples; also KORG logue and Monomachine; GPL-3.0-or-later; author's tool does not change firmware._

_Sources: GitHub README, lapin-list_

### Overwitch

Multitrack Overbridge audio on Linux. Supports Overbridge 2 devices incl. Analog Heat, Heat MKII and Heat +FX, Digitakt I/II, Digitone I/II/Keys, Syntakt. Overbridge 1 devices (Analog Four MKI, Analog Keys, Rytm MKI) not supported. GPL-3.0, 671 commits.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: v2.2 (2025-12-21), GPL-3.0-or-later, JACK clients streaming multitrack Overbridge 2 audio._

_Sources: GitHub README, lapin-list_

### coldfire-rs

Rust stack for ColdFire V4e (MCF5441x): toolchain (rustc_codegen_gcc + libgccjit for m68k-elf), runtime, PAC generated from an SVD, and an Embassy HAL (GPIO, PIT, INTC, eDMA, UART, DSPI, eSDHC eMMC block reads, SSI/I2S, USB OTG device mode). Not an emulator and not an Elektron mod: the README never mentions Elektron or digikit, the only link is the topic tag "digitakt". It is relevant here because digikit names the MCF54415 as the control CPU of Digitakt II (and the Digitone II is described as ColdFire too). Drivers were run on the author's own MCF54415 board. README: API is young and may change before 1.0. 33 commits, Apache-2.0 OR MIT. Same owner also has deluge-sdk (Synthstrom Deluge, out of scope). Org shows no public members; no relation to ElekLabs/Em D found.

_Sources: GitHub README, FirestormAudio profile page_

### elekloader (simonjohansson fork - Digitakt II / Digitone II support)

GitHub says forked from elekloader/elekloader (not irpina's repo); 173 commits, GPL-2.0-or-later, NOTICE covers digikit code. Per README: Digitakt II 1.17 experimental - whole builds and linkable mods with their own core work, core checked in digikit's emulator, a key-swap mod works on a unit. Digitone II 1.12 experimental - whole builds, linkable mods, SHARC (DSP) mods and selectable synth/filter mods work; UI events and remote input checked on a unit, sine variants ran ten-minute note sweeps plus limited project/effects checks. Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 linkable mods with own core, builds with the core work on a unit; Analog Four MKII 1.56 hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit. Issue #13 plans Digitone II control-side support modelled on the Digitakt II implementation (hash-based stock-file recognition, devices/digitakt_mk2.py profile). 22 open issues.

_Related: fork of `elekloader` (GitHub fork flag); vendors `digikit` (catalogue notes: NOTICE covers digikit code) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub README, GitHub issue 13, search 2026-10-31_

### digi-roll-studio

Native Rust desktop sequencer for Digitakt II, Digitone II and Analog Four, built from digi-roll. Writes to hardware: README recommends throwaway projects. Safe-write ceremony of five rules (re-read and back up the destination pattern first, OS build on an allowlist, user confirmation, change only needed bytes, read back and byte-compare). Gen-2 dump protocol (digis) vs gen-1 (Analog Four). +Drive file-write commands 0x57/0x58/0x59 hardware-verified for a single chunk only, not called by the app (writes above 16 KiB refused); 0x5A/0x5B/0x5C (move/copy/delete) not implemented. Protocol code ported from elk-herd (BSD-2, (c) mzero). Fixtures: 34 real .syx dumps. 124 commits, GPL-3.0-or-later. Not firmware modding. Windows/Linux write testing incomplete.

_Related: vendors `elk-herd` (catalogue notes: protocol code ported from elk-herd) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub README, search 2026-10-31_

### digitakt-midi-mcp

MCP server to control a Digitakt II over MIDI (notes, CC, NRPN, transport, raw SysEx) over USB with Overbridge. Includes nrpn_constants.py (full NRPN list per README) and tests that need the physical unit; mappings rest on the manual and the author's code, no independent verification claimed. SysEx tools are experimental and "best-guess" - the README says Elektron has not published the pattern SysEx format. MIT, 46 commits, 11 stars. One of the few agent-facing Elektron tools; relevant model for how an agent can talk to a unit.

_Sources: GitHub README, search 2026-10-31_

### elk-herd

"Elektron device manager". Browser app in Elm for Digitakt and Digitakt II content over Web MIDI: whole-project transfer to and from device and files, reordering of patterns, sample pool and sound pool, renaming (altstrument 2026-11-03; development continues off GitHub, we do not link the new source location). Other projects call it the de-facto public documentation of Elektron's SysEx protocol (digi-roll-studio) and port its 7-bit SysEx codec and F0 00 20 3C framing (SYXGRID). BSD-2-Clause per those projects. The GitHub page is a stub: README says the project has migrated away from GitHub to an obfuscated address (not decoded by us) and that issues and pull requests generated by AI will be summarily rejected - do not open AI-generated ones. Device support is not stated on the stub; SYXGRID says elk-herd does not support the Digitone family; the Digitakt II entry is an inference from digi-roll (which ports its protocol for DT2/DN2). 70 stars.

_Sources: GitHub stub, digi-roll-studio README, SYXGRID README, altstrument (2026-11-03)_

### Elektron Emu

Five VST3 plug-ins (Mac, Windows) that run each machine's real OS in an emulated CPU: Digitakt II, Syntakt, Analog Rytm MKII, Digitone II, Model:Cycles. Firmware not included; the user places the .syx from Elektron's site in a per-machine folder. +Drive emulated and persisted; WAV loading on DT2, Rytm and DN2. Digitone II's DSP is compiled locally on first open (needs a C compiler, else a slow interpreter that renders offline only). Caveats: Rytm analog voices/effects are a custom model that does not sound like the real machine; Syntakt analog tracks 9-12 missing; Mac builds unsigned. 2 commits, 19 stars, no licence stated. Personal project, not affiliated with Elektron (panel photos belong to Elektron).

_Sources: GitHub README, altstrument tools page_

### dt2-capicola (Capicola time stretch for STRETCH/REPITCH/SLICE/GRID)

Custom OS that replaces the Digitakt II's native time-stretch and repitch DSP with an engine built on Heavylight Industries' Capicola (AGPL-3.0-or-later): covers STRETCH, REPITCH, SLICE and GRID; a CAPI parameter switches each track between the new engine and Elektron's; SLICE/GRID sync to tempo and BARS goes to 32. The GitHub repo did not answer on 2026-11-02 (deleted, renamed or private). Its 66 files are kept byte-exact in dt2-machine-lab under machines/capicola-reddit/upstream (pinned from a user-supplied zip, SHA-256 87bb2b07...), which builds its own overlay from it. A comment in its build script says digikit's flash cave 0x403117c4 froze the unit at the logo for that build; other projects use the cave on units (CONFLICTS O18).

_Related: builds on `keyframer-lab` (same Capicola keyframe engine by Heavylight Industries); cites `digikit` (catalogue notes: its build script comments on digikit's flash cave 0x403117c4) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](../PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: dt2-machine-lab machines/capicola-reddit (README and upstream/README.md), read 2026-11-02_

### ElekPrep (elektron-sample-prep)

Single-page browser sample prep: trims at zero crossings, converts to 48 kHz 16-bit WAV, works out loop lengths from BPM and steps; profiles for four devices (device list taken from the related ElekPrep Transfer app, not checked). No MIDI; files go to the unit through Transfer or Elektroid. MIT.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-03), README_

### ElekPrep Transfer

Closed-source browser app that preps audio and sends it over Web MIDI SysEx to the +Drive, with Transfer and +Drive Manager views and device profiles for Digitakt II, Digitakt, Analog Rytm (MKI/MKII) and Model:Samples. Proprietary; author not named. Relation to luizvarela's ElekPrep not established (same name). Interesting as a second independent implementation of +Drive upload over SysEx.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-03)_
